definitions.explanation: A deliberately untrue statement. A formal word implying intentional deception, often used in legal, medical, or serious contexts.

examples.japanese: {虚言|きょげん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{弄|ろう}する。
⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{証言|しょうげん}→証言：11088_shougen⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{虚言|きょげん}だ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{判明|はんめい}→判明：11785_hanmei⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: His testimony was found to be a lie.

examples.japanese: {虚言|きょげん}{癖|へき}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{自分|じぶん}→自分：02887_jibun⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{嘘|うそ}→嘘：01796_uso⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{本当|ほんとう}→本当：00779_hontou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{区別|くべつ}→区別：01555_kubetsu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧つかなくなること⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: People with a tendency to lie may eventually lose the ability to distinguish their own lies from the truth.

notes:
A formal, literary word for lying. Composed of {虚|きょ} (empty, false) + {言|げん} (words, speech). More severe in tone than the everyday word ⟦{嘘|うそ}→嘘：01796_uso⟧.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {虚言|きょげん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{弄|ろう}する: to utter falsehoods (formal)
- {虚言|きょげん}{癖|へき}: a habit of lying; pathological lying
- {虚言|きょげん}{症|しょう}: mythomania, pathological lying (clinical term)
- {虚言|きょげん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{吐|は}く→吐く：04397_haku⟧: to tell lies

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{嘘|うそ}→嘘：01796_uso⟧: lie — the standard everyday word; used in all registers from casual to formal
- ⟦{偽|いつわ}り→偽り：09999_itsuwari⟧: falsehood, deception — literary; implies deliberate deception with a broader scope than just words
- ⟦{虚偽|きょぎ}→虚偽：14047_kyogi⟧: falsehood, untruth — formal/legal; often used for false documents or statements (⟦{虚偽|きょぎ}→虚偽：14047_kyogi⟧⟦{申告|しんこく}→申告：03687_shinkoku⟧: false declaration)

USAGE:
Do not confuse with the homophone ⟦{狂言|きょうげん}→狂言：04456_kyougen⟧, which refers to a traditional Japanese comedic theater form. The readings are close but the pitch accent and kanji are different.
